messages:
Maria Chen: Ran a cross-device perf sweep on model_x (fp16) comparing L4/T4/A10 vs A100/H100. saw a behavioral split around seq=256 that looks like a kernel-path branching bug + KV-cache churn when batches > 8. attaching quick notes.

Maria Chen: summary: L4/T4/A10 pick small GEMM kernels (matmul_small_v3) for seq<=256. those kernels don't stream kv cache well and force repeated KV eviction for mixed-length batches -> 20-30% tail latency blowup vs A100/H100 which pick matmul_large_tile_v1 and keep KV resident.

Maria Chen: perf snippet (from perf-tool):
```
model=model_x fp16 batch=12 seq=192..320
L4: peak_mem=6.8GB, avg_latency=14.2ms, p95=38ms, top_kern=matmul_small_v3
A100: peak_mem=12.1GB, avg_latency=9.1ms, p95=12ms, top_kern=matmul_large_tile_v1
kv-ops: L4 evict_count=420/min, A100 evict_count=18/min
``` 

Devon Li: who changed selector recently? I remember an allocator/heuristic tweak last week — @Ash?

Ash Patel: I landed the "memory-conscious kernel-picker" PR that prefers smaller tile kernels under mem pressure. intended for <8GB cards. It might be overfitting for uniform seq workloads. :thinking:

Priya Kumar: repro command? want to run with `--hotstart` and capture kv-hit-rate trace.

Maria Chen: repro script:
```
./tools/run_profile --model model_x --dtype fp16 --batches 100 --batch-size 12 --seqlen-mix 50:40,256:40,512:20 --trace kv,selector
```

Maria Chen: note: when seqlen mix includes <128 + 512, the small-kernel path thrashes KV because the small kernels allocate compact buffers per step and kernel switching causes cache invalidation. on A100/H100 the large-tile kernel uses persistent buffer and cooperative tiled writes -> much less thrash.

Devon Li: could we modify selector to consider "kv-residency-score" or a penalty for evictions? seems cheaper than reverting the whole change.

Ash Patel: yeah we can add a heuristic: if estimated_evictions_per_token(batch, seqlen_dist) > threshold => prefer larger-tile kernel. need quick cost model.

Priya Kumar: i can run a parameter sweep for thresholds on L4/T4/A10 tomorrow. will push results to the perf board.

Maria Chen: also saw a regression in our CI perf test `seq-256-mix` after the change: +18% latency p95 on T4 matrix. filing a micro-postmortem after we triage.

infra-bot: deployment notice: selector-v2 rolled to canary on gpu-pool-l4 at 2026-03-15T07:42Z. monitor link: https://console.internal/perf/rollouts/selector-v2

Ash Patel: plan: 1) quick revert on selector-v2 for canary pool 2) add kv-penalty heuristic + param sweep 3) bake new preset names: "cross-device-mixedseq-robust-v1" (for <12GB cards) and "high-throughput-tiles-v1" (for >=12GB cards) 4) run bench and gate before rollout.

Maria Chen: agree. can we also dump kernel compile choices (kernel_hash) in traces so we can correlate exact kernel binary across devices?

Devon Li: yes strong +1 to kernel_hash logging. also add per-batch kv-residency metric.

Priya Kumar: i'll schedule the sweep and post results in a follow-up thread. initial hypothesis: threshold ~ 0.15 evictions/token distinguishes when to prefer large-tile kernels on L4/T4/A10.

Ash Patel: thanks team. i'll create a small PR to add the penalty and a quick config toggle for rollout. :thumbsup:

Maria Chen: fyi saved raw traces to s3://redwood-perf/model_x/cross-device/2119876543/ - will attach links in the perf board.

Devon Li: nice work catching this. low-level selectors are tricky with mixed-length traffic.

Maria Chen: tagging QA to run smoke on dedicated: @Priya please add the `seq-mix` CI job to the dedicated gate.

Priya Kumar: on it. will update the job matrix tonight.
